title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Everyone
tiers.description: All Directors, officers, Employees and Contractors, and their family and associates. Bound only by the Insider Trading Ban (paragraphs 8-23) and the Confidential Information obligation (paragraph 44); not by Prohibited Periods, the Clearance Procedures, the margin lending ban, the short term trading ban or the hedging ban.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: All Directors, officers and other Key Management Personnel; Employees at Group Executive, General Manager or Head of level (Tier 8 and above); Company Secretaries; Executive Assistants of Tier 8 and above; nominated Employees and Contractors in Legal, Corporate Affairs, Investor Relations, Finance, Treasury, Strategy, Compliance, Human Resources and Risk Management; and any other person designated by the Chairman, MD & CEO or General Counsel & Company Secretary. All parts of the policy apply.

tiers.name: Chairman of the Board
tiers.description: The Chairman, distinguished only for clearance: the Notification Officer is the Chair of the Audit Committee.

tiers.name: Other Directors
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chairman, including the MD & CEO and alternate Directors. Notification Officer is the Chairman of the Board, and all Directors must confirm completed dealings within 3 business days.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of a Group Company, per AASB 124, including executive and non-executive Directors. Notification Officer is the MD & CEO or the General Counsel & Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Other Company Employees, Contractors
tiers.description: Designated Persons who are neither Directors nor KMP, plus Contractors. Notification Officer is the General Counsel & Company Secretary or the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Associates of Designated Persons
tiers.description: Closely connected persons and entities: family members and dependants, any trustee of a trust or fiduciary arrangement over which the Designated Person has or may be expected to have investment control or influence, companies the Designated Person may control directly or indirectly, nominees, other persons over whom they have investment control or influence, and any other closely related party as defined in the Corporations Act. The policy applies to them, with the notification paragraphs applied as appropriate.

definitions.hedging_definition: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that: i. has not vested in the member; or ii. has vested in the member but remains subject to a holding lock

windows.end_anchor: the start of trading on the first trading day after the Company's half yearly results are announced to ASX
the start of trading on the first trading day after the Company's annual results are announced to ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chairman, MD & CEO or CFO may specify any extension to a closed period and any additional period, conditionally or unconditionally. The Chairman or MD & CEO may also extend the policy to the securities of other specified entities with which the Company has a relationship. The policy does not say whether these are announced or confidential.

rules.detail: Paragraph 31(b) prohibits dealing at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy, and applies to Designated Persons and their closely related parties. Financial Products is defined to include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Company Securities by third parties, with no venue limitation and no vesting qualification, so an OTC put and written call written by a bank are caught. Nothing elsewhere in the policy permits that type of dealing.
rules.evidence: Subject to the law, Designated Persons and their closely related parties (as defined in the Corporations Act) must not: ... b. deal at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy.

rules.detail: Only the Insider Trading Ban and the confidentiality obligation apply to Directors, officers, Employees and Contractors who are not Designated Persons, so the hedging and derivatives prohibitions in paragraph 31 do not reach them. In practice all Directors and KMP are Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: Everyone - including all Directors, officers, Employees and Contractors, and their family and associates | Insider Trading Ban (paragraphs 8-23) and Confidential Information (paragraph 44)

rules.detail: Designated Persons and their closely related parties must not enter into any transaction or arrangement with anyone that could have the effect of limiting exposure to risk relating to unvested remuneration. A put option on variable remuneration is given as an express example of a prohibited arrangement, which is the purchased put leg of a collar.
rules.evidence: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that: i. has not vested in the member ... Examples of prohibited arrangements: a. a put option on variable remuneration;

rules.detail: The same absolute ban extends to remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a holding lock. There is no waiver power; the exceptional circumstances route in Appendix 2 addresses only dealing during a Prohibited Period and disposals.
rules.evidence: ii. has vested in the member but remains subject to a holding lock;

rules.detail: Paragraph 31(a) is confined to unvested and holding-locked remuneration, but paragraph 31(b) is a separate and wider prohibition on dealing at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities. Hedging fully vested, unrestricted shares, whether plan-sourced or bought on market, therefore remains prohibited unless the type of dealing is permitted elsewhere in the policy, and none of the Appendix 1 Permitted Dealings covers a hedge.
rules.evidence: deal at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but forward contracts and swaps are expressly within the definition of Financial Products, so a prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan is caught by the paragraph 31(b) prohibition. A structure with a tenor of less than 30 days would independently breach the short term trading ban, which expressly extends to derivatives and other financial products.
rules.evidence: Financial Products include derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with Company Securities by third parties but do not include portfolio products that are not specific to the Company eg index funds

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling Company Securities. Paragraph 32(b) also gives a short position on remuneration shares as an example of a prohibited hedging arrangement and defines a short position as one where the quantity of shares held is less than the quantity the person is obliged to deliver, which is relevant to any over-hedged or physically settled call position.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short selling of Company Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named. The definition of deal covers taking part in any transaction associated with buying, selling, acquiring, disposing of or converting Company Securities, which does not naturally capture a stock loan, although the resulting short exposure could engage paragraph 32(b).

Contracts for difference are named in the definition of Financial Products, so they are caught by the paragraph 31(b) prohibition on dealing in financial products over Company Securities and by the paragraph 29 ban on short term or speculative trading in derivatives or other financial products.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading in Company Securities or in derivatives or other financial products issued over or in respect of Company Securities.

rules.detail: Margin lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities are prohibited for Designated Persons, on the stated ground that the terms may require Company Securities to be sold during a Prohibited Period or while the person holds Inside Information. Appendix 1 item 6 correspondingly withholds the lender-disposal exclusion from any margin lending agreement prohibited by the policy.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities. The grounds for this include that the terms may require Company Securities to be sold during a Prohibited Period or when the Designated Person possesses Inside Information.

rules.detail: Paragraph 26 binds only Designated Persons; employees and contractors outside that group are not restricted.

Granting security over Company Securities is expressly outside the margin lending prohibition, is not a dealing under the definition of deal, and attracts no notification or disclosure obligation under the policy. Designated Persons are directed to consult the General Counsel & Company Secretary if uncertain whether an arrangement is a margin lending arrangement.
rules.evidence: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where Company Securities may be included as security.

rules.detail: Non-margin secured funding over Company Securities is expressly permitted, with no approval, notification or reporting requirement, and a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is a Permitted Dealing that may occur at any time including during a Prohibited Period, provided the underlying facility is not a prohibited margin lending arrangement. The line between the two is left to the General Counsel & Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where Company Securities may be included as security. Designated Persons should consult the General Counsel & Company Secretary or Company Secretary if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: A 30 day holding period test, expressly extended beyond shares to derivatives and other financial products issued over or in respect of Company Securities, coupled with a ban on speculative trading and a statement that the Company encourages Designated Persons to be long term investors.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading in Company Securities or in derivatives or other financial products issued over or in respect of Company Securities. Short term means in less than a 30 day period.

exemption_authority: The relevant Notification Officer may give prior confirmation, on request, for a Designated Person to deal during a Prohibited Period or to dispose of Company Securities otherwise prohibited under paragraph 24, where Appendix 2 exceptional circumstances exist (severe financial hardship, court order or legal or regulatory requirement, or other circumstances determined by the Chairman, or the MD & CEO where the Chairman is involved). A tax liability does not normally qualify, and the discretion is to be exercised with caution. The relief is expressly limited to paragraph 24 dealings and disposals; there is no power to waive the paragraph 26 margin lending ban, the paragraph 29 short term trading ban or the paragraph 31 hedging and financial products prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Subject to the law, Designated Persons and their closely related parties (as defined in the Corporations Act) must not ... deal at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the clause that defeats the collar: unlike the remuneration hedging ban in 31(a), it is not limited to unvested or locked shares, covers derivatives created by third parties including OTC options, swaps and forwards, and extends to closely related parties, and nothing in Appendix 1 permits a hedge.

bespoke_clauses.clause: except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Read literally, 'permitted by law' could swallow the prohibition, since a collar over vested shares held without inside information is lawful; the drafting is ambiguous and would need a written ruling from the General Counsel & Company Secretary before a bank could rely on it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where Company Securities may be included as security. Designated Persons should consult the General Counsel & Company Secretary or Company Secretary if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on BOQ shares is expressly outside the margin lending ban and needs no approval or disclosure, so the obstacle to a funded collar is the derivative legs, not the financing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Examples of prohibited arrangements: a. a put option on variable remuneration;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The purchased put over plan-sourced shares is the exact structure the policy names as prohibited, so there is no room to argue the ban was not aimed at collars.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale carve-out with a margin lending exception
bespoke_clauses.clause: (lender disposal) a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement if the agreement is prohibited by this policy;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement over the shares by a bank under a permitted, non-margin facility can proceed at any time including in a Prohibited Period, but if the facility were later characterised as a margin loan the executive loses that protection and the enforcement sale becomes a policy breach.

bespoke_clauses.topic: 30 day short term test covering derivatives
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading in Company Securities or in derivatives or other financial products issued over or in respect of Company Securities. Short term means in less than a 30 day period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the derivatives ban were relaxed, any collar or roll with a tenor under 30 days would independently breach the policy, and 'speculative' is undefined.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A confirmation confirms that the proposed dealing by the Designated Person is within the terms of the Securities Trading Policy but does not otherwise constitute approval or endorsement by the Company or the Notification Officer for the proposed dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The clearance is a compliance check with a 3 business day life, not an endorsement, and a Notification Officer cannot confirm a dealing that paragraph 31 prohibits.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associates of a Designated Person include ... any trustee of a trust or other fiduciary arrangement under which a Designated Person has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence, companies in which a Designated Person may control directly or indirectly, nominees ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the collared parcel through a trust, nominee or controlled company does not avoid paragraph 31, which binds closely related parties directly.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any extension to a closed period, and any additional period (conditionally or unconditionally), as specified by the Chairman, MD & CEO or CFO of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Three officers can extend or add Prohibited Periods conditionally at short notice, so any structure requiring a dealing on a fixed future date carries timing risk.

summary: A funded collar is not available to a BOQ Designated Person, which includes every Director and member of Key Management Personnel. The obstacle is paragraph 31(b), a standalone prohibition on Designated Persons and their closely related parties dealing at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, where Financial Products is defined to include derivatives, options, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference created by third parties; unlike the remuneration hedging ban in 31(a) it is not limited to unvested or holding-locked shares, and a put option is expressly named as a prohibited arrangement. The financing leg, by contrast, is unusually accommodating: paragraph 26 bans only margin lending, paragraph 27 expressly states that the restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where Company Securities may be included as security, and Appendix 1 item 6 lets a secured lender enforce at any time, including during a Prohibited Period, provided the facility is not a prohibited margin loan. The only route to a collar would be a written ruling from the General Counsel & Company Secretary that it is a 'type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy' within the closing words of paragraph 31(b), which is a genuine ambiguity but a thin basis for a bank to lend against, and no exemption power exists since the Appendix 2 exceptional circumstances relief reaches only paragraph 24 dealings and disposals. Even then the 30 day short term trading test, which expressly covers derivatives, and the Front Page Test would apply.
